body.name: \operatorname{LP}_{m,h,s}^{\mathrm{int}}(\lambda)
body.construction: Fix integers \(m,s\ge1\) and a grid \(G_h=\{-r=\rho_0<\cdots<\rho_J=r\}\) with rational or computable-real nodes and maximum adjacent gap at most \(h\). Let \(\mathsf X_m=\{(k,l)\in\mathbb N_0^2:k+l\le m\}\), append an overflow state \(\star\), and let \(\tau_m(\lambda)=\Pr\{\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)>m\}\). For \(m+1>\lambda\), certify the discarded mass by \[\tau_m(\lambda)\le \overline\tau_m(\lambda):=e^{-\lambda}\left(\frac{e\lambda}{m+1}\right)^{m+1};\] its worst effects are at most \(\overline\tau_m\) on coverage and \(2br\overline\tau_m\) on expected length. The finite action grid is \(\mathsf A_h=\{[a-b\rho_v,a-b\rho_u]:0\le u\le v\le J\}\); the lower relaxation additionally admits a null grid-coverage pattern of length zero. For any rule and \(\rho,\rho'\in[-r,r]\), the common-count coupling gives \[\lVert f_{\lambda,\rho}-f_{\lambda,\rho'}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\omega_\lambda(|\rho-\rho'|):=\min\{1,\lambda c|\rho-\rho'|/2\},\] and hence every fixed event has probability modulus \(\omega_\lambda\), while every \([0,2br]\)-valued length has expectation modulus \(2br\omega_\lambda\). The lower finite LP uses variables \(w_{x,A}\) for \(x\in\mathsf X_m\), row sums one, gridwise retained-state coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\tau_m\), and gridwise retained expected length at most \(t\). It is a relaxation because an arbitrary interval maps to the shortest action spanning exactly the grid targets it covers, and overflow can contribute at most \(\tau_m\) to coverage. The upper finite LP uses \(\mathsf A_h\), fixes \(A_\star=\mathcal A\), and imposes gridwise coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) and expected length at most \(t\). Its rule expands each \(A=[L,U]\) to \(E_h(A)=[\max\{a-br,L-bh/2\},\min\{a+br,U+bh/2\}]\), which adds at most \(bh\) in length and makes coverage of the nearest grid target imply coverage of \(a-b\rho\). Put \(\omega_h=\min\{1,\lambda ch/4\}\) and \(\gamma_h=\omega_h/(\alpha+\omega_h)\); mixing the expanded rule with the full interval \(\mathcal A\) with probability \(\gamma_h\) repairs its off-grid coverage from \(1-\alpha-\omega_h\) to at least \(1-\alpha\), and adds at most \(2br\gamma_h\) in length. Computation at an arbitrary real \(\lambda\) supplied as a computable input uses an oracle returning rationals \(\lambda_s^-\le\lambda\le\lambda_s^+\) with \(\lambda_s^+-\lambda_s^-\le2^{-s}\); the same rational-or-oracle encoding is used for fixed real inputs. Directed interval evaluation of the exponential, powers, probabilities, action lengths, and all remaining coefficients returns rational bounds \(f_{s,j,x}^-\le f_{\lambda,\rho_j}(x)\le f_{s,j,x}^+\), \(\tau_{m,s}^-\le\tau_m(\lambda)\le\tau_{m,s}^+\le\overline\tau_m(\lambda_s^+)\), and outward upper bounds for \(\omega_h,bh,2br\omega_h,2br\gamma_h\). In the rational lower relaxation, coverage uses \(f^+\) and right side \(1-\alpha-\tau^+\), while length uses \(f^-\); any exactly rational dual-feasible vector, checked by integer arithmetic after clearing denominators, gives a value \(D_{m,h,s}^-\le C_\alpha(\lambda)\). In the rational upper restriction, coverage uses \(f^-\) and \(\tau^-\), while length uses \(f^+\) and \(\tau^+\); any exactly rational primal-feasible vector gives \(P_{m,h,s}^+\), and the reported upper certificate is \(U_{m,h,s}^+=P_{m,h,s}^++bh+2br\omega_h+2br\gamma_h\), with every displayed correction replaced computationally by its directed rational upper enclosure. Thus \(\operatorname{LP}_{m,h,s}^{\mathrm{int}}(\lambda)\) reports the rational enclosure \([D_{m,h,s}^-,U_{m,h,s}^+]\); floating-point solvers may propose witnesses but only the exactly checked rational primal and dual witnesses constitute the certificate. Along any refinement with \(m\to\infty\), \(h\downarrow0\), \(s\to\infty\), and \(m+1>\lambda_s^+\), the tail, mesh, repair, and coefficient-enclosure errors vanish.
